label: copy-phase input token g
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), on steps whose input (the token just copied back) is g. Never fires on g in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. Recall is 100%; ~20% of copy-phase g inputs stay inactive, mostly when g is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, rate 1.5% vs ~3% later) or in short sequences. Magnitude is lowest when g is copied early (first copy step) and highest late in long sequences (top examples are g copied right before the end of an L=9 sequence); a second consecutive g gets a smaller activation than the first.

issues: Core claims hold. The feature fires only in the copy phase (original 0, delimiter 0), only when in_tok is g (lift 32x on g, 0 on every other token), and recall on test is 1.0 with 0 missed activations. Magnitude rising with t and L is consistent with the profile, and mass share grows with L.

The explanation misstates the recall_idx-1 numbers. The quoted '1.5% vs about 3%' are overall per-step firing rates over all tokens at each recall_idx, not rates for g inputs. Conditioned on input g, recall_idx==1 fires 46% of the time (dev precision 0.458, n=16788), against about 87% for recall_idx>=2. So the first copied g is a much bigger false-positive source than the explanation implies.

There is a systematic false-positive class the predicate ignores: the first copied g in short sequences. Firing rate depends strongly on L at recall_idx==1: 0.073 at L=4, 0.381 at L=6, 0.829 at L=9. Over (recall_idx==1)&(L<=5) the rate is 0.139. By absolute step t, g fires 0.092 of the time at t=5, 0.52 at t=6, 0.62 at t=7, and 0.84-0.87 at t>=9. L==3 fires only 0.10, and (recall_idx==3)&(L==4) is 0.53. The feature effectively needs some time after <DEL> (late absolute t) before it turns on for g. The explanation's 'plus short sequences' hints at this but the predicate does not capture it.

The alternative the other agent tried (recall_idx>=2) was the wrong cut. It drops first-copied g in long sequences, which do fire (0.83 at L=9). An L-dependent exclusion does better: ~((recall_idx==1)&(L<=6)) gives test P 0.856, R 0.975, F1 0.911, mass recall 0.991, against the original's F1 0.886. Even the simple t>=6 cut gives test F1 0.901.

The leftover false positives under the refined predicate (about 14%) look scattered across positions and lengths, i.e. noise. The leftover misses are small activations (0.9% of mass) on the first copied g at L=5-6.
The label 'copy-phase input token g' is fine as a label. The predicate and explanation should note that it is suppressed on early copy steps (first copied g when L<=6, or t<=5).
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input token g (suppressed on the first copied g in short sequences)

final_label: copy-phase input token g (suppressed on the first copied g in short sequences)
